title: Counit-compatible shift structure of derived change of rings on a site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of its module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Write $K(R)$ for the homotopy category of complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $Q_R:K(R)\to D(R)$ and $Q_S:K(S)\to D(S)$ for the localizations at quasi-isomorphisms, and $s_P:Q_R(P[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Q_RP)[1]$, $s'_M:Q_S(M[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Q_SM)[1]$ for their shift isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $(P[1])^r=P^{r+1}$ and $d_{P[1]}=-d_P$. Let $E:K(R)\to K(S)$ be termwise change of rings $P\mapsto P\otimes_RS$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and let $\theta_P:E(P[1])\to E(P)[1]$ be the identity in every degree (both complexes have $P^{r+1}\otimes_RS$ in degree $r$ and differential $-d_P\otimes1$). Let $F=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RS:D(R)\to D(S)$ be the derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with its derived counit $\varepsilon:F\circ Q_R\to Q_S\circ E$, the natural transformation of the left derived functor of $Q_S\circ E$ [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Then there is a unique family of isomorphisms $\sigma_X:F(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(X)[1]$, natural in $X\in D(R)$, such that for every complex $P$ of $R$-modules
$$\varepsilon_P[1]\circ\sigma_{Q_RP}\circ F(s_P)=s'_{E(P)}\circ Q_S(\theta_P)\circ\varepsilon_{P[1]}:\ F(Q_R(P[1]))\to(Q_SE(P))[1],$$
and with this family $(F,\sigma)$ is a triangulated functor [def-weil-triangulated-category]: for every distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$ of $D(R)$ the triangle $F(X)\xrightarrow{F(u)}F(Y)\xrightarrow{F(v)}F(Z)\xrightarrow{\sigma_X\circ F(w)}F(X)[1]$ is distinguished in $D(S)$. No flatness of $S$ over $R$ and no boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the smallness hypothesis makes both sheaf-module categories abelian. Their homotopy categories and the localization functors have the cone triangulations of [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Termwise tensor is additive: on local tensor generators its map sends $m\otimes s$ to $f(m)\otimes s$, so it preserves sums of maps. It preserves the biproduct identities and hence the biproduct $L^r\oplus P^{r+1}$ in the cone formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Under this identification its cone differential is $\begin{pmatrix}d_L\otimes1&f\otimes1\\0&-d_P\otimes1\end{pmatrix}$, exactly the cone differential of $E(f)$. If $f-g=dh+hd$, then $E(f)-E(g)=dE(h)+E(h)d$, so it descends to homotopy categories. The cone inclusion and negative projection are preserved as well. Thus $E$ carries cone triangles to cone triangles; since distinguished triangles are their isomorphic copies, $E$, and then $B:=Q_S\circ E$, are exact.

source.place: Definitions 05RR, 05RU and the cone construction in Section 13.11; literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex, Tag 03EK

proof.text: Take the resolving class to be K-flat complexes with flat terms. Every complex has such a quasi-isomorphic resolution by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] says that termwise change of rings sends every quasi-isomorphism between these complexes to a quasi-isomorphism, so $B$ inverts these arrows. The two hypotheses of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] therefore hold for $B:K(R)\to D(S)$. It supplies the everywhere-defined left derived functor $F$, the counit $\varepsilon:F\circ Q_R\to B$ with its right Kan universal property, and invertibility of $\varepsilon_P$ on the resolving class. This is the derived tensor functor of clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Neither resolution existence nor clause (1) requires flatness of $S$ over $R$ or boundedness.

For every $P$, both $E(P[1])$ and $E(P)[1]$ have degree-$r$ term $P^{r+1}\otimes_R S$ and differential $-d_P\otimes1$. Hence the degreewise identities give the natural isomorphism $\theta_P$. For an integer shift $n$, replace $1$ by $n$ and the minus sign by $(-1)^n$; composition of these identities gives the zero and addition coherence identities. Together with the localization shift structure, this gives the coherent shift comparison of $B=Q_S\circ E$, whose degree-one component is $b_P=s'_{E(P)}\circ Q_S(\theta_P):B(P[1])\to B(P)[1]$.

source.place: Tag 05SU(2), together with the complex-shift definition in Section 13.11 and the termwise tensor construction in sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-right-kan-extension-coherent-shift] with source $K(R)$, localization $Q_R:K(R)\to D(R)$, original functor $B=Q_S\circ E:K(R)\to D(S)$, right Kan extension $F$, and counit $\varepsilon$. Here the functor in that theorem with codomain $D(S)$ is $B$, rather than $E$ with codomain $K(S)$. The preceding steps provide the coherent shifts of $Q_R$ and $B$ and the required universal property. The theorem gives coherent natural isomorphisms $\sigma_X:F(X[1])\to F(X)[1]$ making $\varepsilon$ commute with shifts. Expanding that assertion at $P$, using the component $b_P$ computed above, gives precisely $\varepsilon_P[1]\circ\sigma_{Q_RP}\circ F(s_P)=s'_{E(P)}\circ Q_S(\theta_P)\circ\varepsilon_{P[1]}$.

source.place: Tag 05SU(2) and Proposition 05SE, LF part; generic universal-property formulation

proof.text: For uniqueness no coherence assumption on a competing family is needed. Put $H(X)=F(X[1])[-1]$. A natural family $\sigma$ determines a transformation $a^\sigma:H\to F$ with component $\sigma_X[-1]$, using the canonical inverse-shift identifications. If $\sigma$ and $\tau$ satisfy the displayed counit equation, shifting that equation by $[-1]$ and cancelling the common isomorphism $F(s_P)[-1]$ shows $\varepsilon_P\circ a^\sigma_{Q_RP}=\varepsilon_P\circ a^\tau_{Q_RP}$ for every $P$. Injectivity of the universal correspondence for the test functor $H$, stated in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], gives $a^\sigma=a^\tau$. Applying $[1]$ gives $\sigma=\tau$.

Let $\Delta=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$ be distinguished in $D(R)$. By [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated] the quasi-isomorphisms $W$ of $K(R)$ are a saturated triangulated multiplicative system (so right calculus of fractions and two-out-of-three hold) and $Q_R$ is the shift-compatible localization at $W$. By [lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy] for $B$, $W$ and the K-flat flat-term class (its two hypotheses are those of step 2), the denominator diagram of $B$ is essentially constant at every complex. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-kan-source-triangles] with $D=K(R)$, $D'=D(S)$, $L=D(R)$, exact $B$ (step 1), $Q=Q_R$, $LF=F$ with $\sigma$ (step 4) and $\alpha=\varepsilon$, a right Kan extension (step 2) commuting with shifts (step 4): for every distinguished $T=(K\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}N\xrightarrow{h}K[1])$ of $K(R)$, $F(Q_RK)\to F(Q_RM)\to F(Q_RN)\xrightarrow{\sigma_{Q_RK}F(s_KQ_Rh)}F(Q_RK)[1]$ is distinguished, i.e. $(F,\sigma)$ maps $Q_R(T)$ to a distinguished triangle. By [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6] (its triangulation is that of $D(R)$, by uniqueness) there is a triangle isomorphism $(a,b,c):\Delta\to Q_R(T)$, with last arrow $w'$ of $Q_R(T)$. Then $(Fa,Fb,Fc)$ is a triangle isomorphism from $(FX,FY,FZ,Fu,Fv,\sigma_XF(w))$ to the image of $Q_R(T)$: the first two squares are $F$ of those of $(a,b,c)$, and $F(a)[1]\sigma_XF(w)=\sigma F(a[1])F(w)=\sigma F(w')F(c)$ by naturality of $\sigma$. By (TR1) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] the first triangle is distinguished. $F$ is additive, being exact by [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Hence $(F,\sigma)$ is exact with the comparison of the statement, not merely some comparison.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q105-9693d743d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all six steps in full, the statements of all 12 cited nodes, unit sk-rem-rest (a remark with no steps, so no route), the reviewed parent lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-unit-triangles, Stacks derived.tex 05SU (l.4657) and 05SE (l.4895), sites-cohomology.tex 06YY (l.3585), and the main-20261015 prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations proof Step 1. The statement is true, and its coefficient categories match 06YY: R- and S-module sheaves on a small site, unbounded, with no flatness or boundedness assumed. The displayed equation is exactly the condition that the counit ε commutes with shifts. Edge cases checked: S=0, R=S, P=0, unbounded P. The delivery has no new nodes. I searched for duplicates (counit/shift, derived change of rings, 05SU) and found none.

Steps 1-5 are correct as written. Step 1: the termwise tensor preserves the cone matrix and homotopies. Step 2: both hypotheses of lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class hold, from lem-pc-kflat-resolution and clause (1) of lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings. Step 3: θ is the identity in every degree. Step 4: lem-pur-right-kan-extension-coherent-shift applies to B=Q_S∘E, and expanding its conclusion gives the displayed equation. Step 5: uniqueness follows from injectivity of the Kan correspondence for H=[-1]F[1].

One fault, C3/C4, in step 6. The step took exactness from lem-pur-left-derived-exact-when-defined, whose statement never says which shift comparison it uses. It then identified that comparison with the step-4 σ by step 5's uniqueness. But step 5 only applies to comparisons already known to satisfy the counit equation, and that fact is in the cited node's proof, not its statement. The point matters: with -σ the image triangles are not distinguished. I rewrote step 6 using statements only. lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated and lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy give essential constancy. lem-pur-left-derived-kan-source-triangles, applied with σ from step 4, makes images of homotopy-category triangles distinguished. lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6 (Mathlib leaf) and TR1 extend this to every triangle, with the third square written out from naturality of σ. proof_deps and tool_uses are updated: lem-pur-left-derived-exact-when-defined is dropped, kan-source-triangles and resolving-class-essential-constancy are added. I checked that the new citations create no cycle. All other declared tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes, since the remark unit has no route.
